entities.label: Fereydun

entities.label: Shahrnaz
entities.summary: A wife of Fereydun, mother of his two elder sons.

facts.text: Mother of two sons of Fereydun

entities.label: Arnavaz

facts.text: Mother of the youngest son of Fereydun

entities.summary: The eldest son of Fereydun.

entities.label: Iraj

entities.label: Jandal
entities.summary: A trusted and eloquent noble whom Fereydun sends to find brides for his sons.

entities.label: Sarv

entities.summary: Three sisters of one father and one mother, the daughters of the king of Yemen.

entities.summary: The land of the Turks and Chin, which Fereydun gives to Tur.

entities.label: The mobad sent by Salm and Tur
entities.summary: A shrewd and eloquent mobad whom the two brothers send to their father.

entities.label: Mah-Afarid
entities.summary: A handmaiden in the household of Iraj, whom Iraj loved.

entities.label: The daughter of Iraj

entities.label: Pashang
entities.summary: The husband Fereydun chooses for the daughter of Iraj; not the king of Turan of the same name.

facts.text: Husband of the daughter of Iraj

entities.label: Manuchehr
entities.summary: The grandson of Iraj, raised and taught by Fereydun.

entities.label: Qaren
entities.summary: A commander of the army, named in the poem as Qaren of the house of Kaveh.

entities.label: Shiruy
entities.summary: A warrior and leader of the army, called a lion-slayer.

entities.label: Sam
entities.summary: A hero, son of Nariman, among the leaders of the army.

entities.label: Shapur
entities.summary: A warrior of the court of Fereydun.

entities.label: The envoy seeking pardon
entities.summary: An eloquent man whom Salm and Tur send to Fereydun with gifts.

entities.label: The Kaviani banner
entities.summary: The banner of the kings of Iran.

entities.label: Tamisha
entities.summary: The seat of Fereydun, from which the army marches out.

entities.label: The fortress of Alanan
entities.summary: A fortress behind the army of Salm and Tur, rising from the water.

entities.label: Qobad
entities.summary: A warrior who leads the vanguard of Manuchehr.

entities.label: Garshasp
entities.summary: A warrior who commands the left wing of the army; not the later king of that name.

entities.label: The keeper of the fortress
entities.summary: The keeper of the fortress of Alanan.

entities.label: The ring of Tur
entities.summary: The seal ring of Tur.

entities.label: Sari

events.label: Three sons
events.summary: When Fereydun is fifty, three sons are born to him, tall as cypresses and like their father in all things; the two elder are of Shahrnaz, the youngest of Arnavaz. Their father has not yet given them names.

events.label: Jandal's search
events.summary: Fereydun sends Jandal to find three sisters of one father and one mother, worthy of his sons. Jandal searches every land and finds them only with Sarv, the king of Yemen, to whom he delivers Fereydun's proposal.

events.label: Sarv takes counsel
events.summary: Sarv is grieved at the thought of losing his daughters but fears to refuse a king who brought down Zahhak. His chiefs tell him that they are no one's slaves and that, if he fears Fereydun, he should ask for things that cannot be done.

events.label: Sarv's answer
events.summary: Sarv tells Jandal that he will obey, but that the three princes must come to him so that he can see them himself before he gives them his daughters. Jandal brings the answer back.

events.label: A father's counsel
events.summary: Fereydun tells his sons of the king of Yemen and his daughters and urges them to answer wisely and truthfully, for the king of Yemen is a deep thinker. The three set out, full of knowledge.

events.label: The brides
events.summary: The three princes reach Yemen with priests and an army and are welcomed with jewels and musk. Sarv gives them his three daughters, saying bitterly to himself that ill has come to him from Fereydun, and the princes set out for home.

events.label: The world divided
events.summary: Fereydun divides the world in three. Salm receives Rum and the West, Tur the land of the Turks and Chin, called Turan, and Iraj Iran and the plains of the spear-bearers, with the royal throne and crown. Each takes his throne in peace.

events.label: Salm's envy
events.summary: As Fereydun grows old, greed stirs in Salm: he cannot bear that the youngest brother has the golden throne. He sends word to Tur that their father has wronged them both, and Tur, angered, agrees that they must act without delay.

events.label: A harsh message
events.summary: The two brothers meet and send a mobad to their father: he has favoured one son over the others; let him take the crown from Iraj and give him a corner of the world, or they will bring the armies of Turan, Chin and Rum against Iran.

events.label: Fereydun's reply
events.summary: At Fereydun's court, the mobad delivers the message. Fereydun answers that he divided the world with the counsel of the wise and in fear of God, and warns his sons that whoever sends a brother to the dust is no true son of his line.

events.label: Iraj chooses peace
events.summary: Fereydun warns Iraj of his brothers' hostility and urges him to prepare. Iraj replies that he wants no throne at the cost of hatred: he will go to his brothers without an army and win them back with kindness. Fereydun praises his wisdom but fears for him, and promises to write to them.

events.label: A letter and a journey
events.summary: Fereydun writes to Salm and Tur that their brother, who longed to see them, has left his throne and comes to them as a servant, and asks them to honour him and send him back. Iraj sets out with a few companions.

events.label: The army looks at Iraj
events.summary: The brothers receive Iraj with false warmth. Their soldiers cannot take their eyes off him and whisper that he alone is worthy to be king. Salm sees it and tells Tur that unless Iraj is uprooted he will throw them from their thrones; they spend the night plotting.

events.label: The death of Iraj
events.summary: In the tent Tur asks why the youngest should wear the crown. Iraj answers that he wants neither Iran nor any kingdom and gives up the crown to them. Unmoved, Tur strikes him with a golden chair; Iraj begs for his life, but Tur kills him with a dagger, cuts off his head, fills it with musk and sends it to their father.

entityAssociations.role: father to whom the head is sent

events.label: The golden coffin
events.summary: While Fereydun prepares a triumphant welcome for Iraj, a mourner arrives with a golden coffin holding the severed head. Fereydun falls from his horse; the army tears its garments and returns in black. In Iraj's garden he burns the trees and prays to live until an avenger of Iraj's seed arises, weeping until grass grows around him and his eyes grow dark.

events.label: Mah-Afarid's child
events.summary: Fereydun finds that Mah-Afarid, whom Iraj loved, is carrying his child, and takes hope. A daughter is born who looks like Iraj; when she is grown, Fereydun gives her in marriage to Pashang, and she bears a son.

events.label: Manuchehr
events.summary: The boy is brought to Fereydun, who rejoices as if Iraj lived again; his sight returns and he names the child Manuchehr. He raises him with every care, teaches him the arts of kings, and gives him his golden throne, his mace, his crown and his treasures; the nobles hail him, with Qaren and Shiruy among the leaders of the army.

events.label: An offer of atonement
events.summary: Alarmed by the news, Salm and Tur send an eloquent envoy with elephants and treasure. He says the brothers repent, blame fate and the demon, and ask that Manuchehr come to them so that they may serve him and pay the blood-price of his grandfather.

events.label: Fereydun refuses
events.summary: Fereydun sees through the offer: if they love Manuchehr, where is Iraj? They will see him only at the head of an army, with the Kaviani banner and heroes such as Qaren, Shapur, Shiruy and Sam.

events.label: The brothers march
events.summary: The envoy returns and describes the splendour of Fereydun's court and the strength of Manuchehr. Tur tells Salm that the lion's cub must not be allowed to grow, and the two lead their armies from the West towards Iran.

events.label: Manuchehr leads the army
events.summary: Fereydun sends Manuchehr out with the army. From Tamisha it marches under the Kaviani banner: Garshasp on the left, Sam and Qobad on the right, Manuchehr in the centre, with Qaren leading. Salm and Tur draw up their forces with the fortress of Alanan behind them.

events.label: Tur's taunt
events.summary: Tur tells Qobad to ask the new king, who has no father, who gave him sword and armour, since he descends from Iraj only through a daughter. Qobad warns him he will regret his words; Manuchehr laughs and says that God and Fereydun know Iraj is his forefather, and the battle will show his lineage.

events.label: The night proclamation
events.summary: At nightfall a herald cries through the army of Qaren that this is a war against evil: whoever dies in it will be pure for paradise, and whoever wins will have fame, land and reward. The chiefs swear to obey.

events.label: The first battle
events.summary: At dawn Manuchehr leads out the army and the two hosts clash until the plain is a sea of blood. The day is with Manuchehr; at nightfall Salm and Tur think of a night attack.

events.label: The night raid
events.summary: Spies tell Manuchehr of the planned raid. He leaves the army with Qaren and waits in ambush with thirty thousand men. When Tur comes by night, he finds the army ready and turns to flee; Manuchehr overtakes him, throws him from his saddle with a spear and cuts off his head.

events.label: A head for Fereydun
events.summary: Manuchehr writes to Fereydun of the three battles and the death of Tur, and sends him Tur's head, as Tur once sent Iraj's. Fereydun weeps, and blesses Manuchehr.

events.label: The fortress taken by a ring
events.summary: Qaren guesses that Salm will retreat to the fortress of Alanan. Taking Tur's ring, he goes alone to the keeper of the fortress as Tur's messenger and is let in; at dawn he raises a banner as a sign, Shiruy storms the gate, and the fortress burns.

events.label: The death of Salm
events.summary: Salm flees towards the fortress but finds no ship at the shore. Manuchehr overtakes him, reproaches him for killing his brother for a crown, and cuts him in two with his sword; Salm's head is raised on a spear.

events.label: Mercy for the defeated
events.summary: Salm's army sends a wise man to say that they are herdsmen and farmers who came at their lords' command and now submit. Manuchehr forbids further bloodshed, takes their arms and honours them, and sends Shiruy to bring the treasure of the fortress.

events.label: Manuchehr crowned
events.summary: The victorious army returns by way of Sari to Tamisha. Fereydun comes out to meet it; Manuchehr dismounts and kisses the ground, and Fereydun, thanking God for justice done, has him sit on the golden throne with the crown.

events.label: The death of Fereydun
events.summary: His work done, Fereydun withdraws from the throne with the heads of his three sons before him and weeps until his life ends. Manuchehr puts on the crown, girds himself in mourning and builds him a royal tomb of gold and lapis.
